variant_assignment_id.description: Permanent split assignment ID as a decimal string, present only for split activities

ContactCreate.description: At least one nonblank first_name, last_name, or username is required. Organization comes from authentication.

followers.description: Nonnegative integer with at most 255 decimal digits.

inbox_agent_user_id.description: Active, assignable user in the connected organization. Discover IDs with GET /assignee.

last_message_on.description:
Last message time; omitted or null defaults to the contact's creation time.
Use a full ISO 8601 timestamp with seconds and Z or an explicit UTC offset,
such as 2026-11-17T10:15:30-08:00. Values are converted to UTC and fractional
seconds are discarded. The resulting UTC year must be 1000 through 9999.
Dates without a time or timestamps without a timezone are rejected.

origin.description: Source of this contact; saved in contact JSON metadata.

profile_image_url.description:
Public HTTP(S) avatar URL. No restriction on pixel dimensions.
Hard limit 5 MB (5 MiB / 5242880 bytes), checked during download; larger files
fail creation. Raster bytes are copied without
resizing to meta-profile-pics/profile-pics/{generated identifier}.jpg.
Supported raster signatures are JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, TIFF, AVIF.
SVG is rejected. Only public hosts on ports 80 or 443 are allowed.

source_image_url.description: HTTP(S) image or thumbnail associated with the contact's original touchpoint, without embedded credentials. Saved in contact JSON metadata after trimming; the image is not downloaded or copied.

source_name.description: Where the contact first engaged, such as a post, reel, ad, SMS, or email. Caller-provided free text saved in contact JSON metadata.

contact.description: Saved contact fields, including id, profile_pic (stored S3 URL), and actual stored timestamps in UTC with Z.

assignee_id.description:
ID of the assignee to assign.
Must be a valid user ID in your organization.
Use GET /assignee to retrieve available assignee IDs.

custom_fields.description: Any additional custom fields defined for the contact

label_id.description:
ID of the label to assign.
Use GET /label to retrieve available label IDs.

status_id.description:
ID of the status to assign.
Use GET /status to retrieve available status IDs.

contactId.description: Optional existing Ellipsend contact ID in the authenticated organization. Does not create a contact.

eventId.description: Unique external event identity. Reuse it for retries of the same event.

payload.description: JSON event data up to 64 KiB. Fields become event.payload Liquid variables. Do not include credentials.

resultKey.description: Optional capture name; constructor and prototype are reserved and cannot be used.

revision.description: The immutable saved version from exported request.revision. Update explicitly after editing the saved request.

stepId.description: Stable action position; defaults to the saved request UUID. Keep it unchanged on retries.

executionId.description: Durable execution identifier, when a receipt has been allocated.

variables.description: Values captured according to the saved request's result configuration.

info.description:
# ![Ellipsend Logo](https://ellipsend.com/Public/images/Ellipsend-LOGO-SOCIAL-GRADIENT.svg)

API for managing statuses, labels, assignees, contacts and saved HTTP request executions.

## Authentication
Obtain an access token from `POST /v1/auth/token` using your Ellipsend
`client_id` and `client_secret`, or use your existing Ellipsend API token.
Send the token in `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` for protected operations.

## Run a saved HTTP request
Open **Settings → Integrations → HTTP requests** in Ellipsend, configure the
outgoing request and select **Save request**. Then choose **More → Export JSON**
(the download icon on wide screens). The exported `request.id` is the UUID
used in the execution URL; `request.revision` is the saved version sent in
the request body. Save before exporting: export includes the current editor
values and an unsaved draft is not an executable saved version.

Call `POST /v1/http-requests/{requestId}/execute` with that UUID, revision,
a stable `eventId` and your event data. The saved outgoing request can use
`{{ event.payload.email }}` or other fields from `payload`. Reuse the same
event ID and step ID for retries. An ordinary contact/activity API operation
requires a separate execution call to run a saved HTTP request.

Results are visible in **HTTP requests → Activity**. Saved provider credentials
stay in the saved connection; do not include them in event data.

## Rate Limits
- Global rate limit: 100 requests per second
- Auth endpoints (/auth/*): 10 requests per minute
- All other endpoints follow the global rate limit

post.description:
Creates a contact in the organization of the authenticated API connection.
At least one nonblank first_name, last_name, or username is required;
all other fields are optional. Both follow flags default to false.
organization_id is stored from authentication and cannot be supplied.
Each call creates a new contact and does not open a messaging window.
last_message_on defaults to the contact's creation time. Explicit values
require a full ISO 8601 timestamp with Z or an offset such as -08:00.
Timestamps are stored in UTC to whole seconds and returned with Z.

Profile images have a hard file limit of 5 MB (5 MiB / 5242880 bytes),
including streamed downloads. There is no restriction on pixel dimensions.
Images are copied without resizing or
transcoding to existing profile image storage. Oversized images fail creation.

post.description:
**Setup:** Save the outgoing request in **Settings → Integrations → HTTP requests**,
then choose **More → Export JSON** (download icon on wide screens).
Use exported `request.id` for `requestId` and `request.revision` for `revision`.
A newly saved request starts at revision 1. Editing and saving creates a
new immutable revision; an existing integration keeps its pinned revision
until you update the revision in its call.

The full URL is `https://api.ellipsend.com/v1/http-requests/{requestId}/execute`.
Use your **Ellipsend** bearer token, not the destination provider's token.
Organization and API-user identity come from authentication; the saved
request must be enabled and belong to that organization.

`payload.email` is available to the outgoing Liquid template as
`{{ event.payload.email }}`; the event ID is `{{ event.id }}`.
Optional `contactId` loads an existing contact's fields for `{{ contact.email }}`
and other contact variables. This operation does not create a contact.

A contact/activity create or update does not automatically execute a saved
request. Make this separate call when that operation succeeds.

Use a new `eventId` for each distinct external event. For a retry, preserve
the same `requestId` and complete JSON body, including optional fields. A duplicate
execution returns the durable receipt rather than resending the request.
Only `receipt.outcome: success` confirms completion. For HTTP 202 with
accepted/unknown outcome, stop dependent actions and reuse the original
identity to check the receipt; do not generate a new ID to retry blindly.

Destination credentials come from the saved connection. Credential fields,
organization/actor overrides and arbitrary destination URLs are not accepted
in this event. Event and receipt bodies are excluded from API request logs.
Review execution details in **HTTP requests → Activity**.

200.description: Confirmed successful execution; JSON contains the durable receipt.

202.description: Accepted or unknown receipt; stop dependent actions and reuse the same event identity.

400.description: Invalid revision, event identity, JSON data or credential/identity override.

422.description: Confirmed failure; JSON contains the durable failure receipt.
